second_order: testing what counts as a good April Fools joke
theme_note: People post, recognise, praise, criticise, explain, and extend jokes played in or discussed by the room; what varies is whether the joke is admired, judged mistimed, or called poor.

second_order: calling people to put up a Singapore flag
theme_note: People recruit helpers, name targets, supply coordinates, and commit to attempts; the proposed target and location keep changing.
People ask what the canvas or a neighbouring drawing is and others explain the pixel timer, location, or group behind it.
People turn flag calls, neighbouring colours, haze, and nation-building into jokes while the canvas work continues.

second_order: arguing over whether a flag is worth the effort
theme_note: People compare participation, priorities, and national loyalty while disputing why the room should make or yield a flag.

second_order: working out where and how to make the flag
theme_note: People relocate, sketch, choose borders and coordinates, correct shapes, and circulate heart or skyline plans; the design and site vary across attempts.

second_order: reporting the flag being lost, weak, or under pressure
theme_note: People report overwritten stars, griefing, destruction, failed attempts, numerical weakness, and disputed completion; accounts vary from brief survival to denying a whole flag ever existed.

second_order: negotiating and contesting room on the canvas
theme_note: People warn, object, seek truces, ask permission, propose alliances, and answer claims by neighbouring groups; what varies is whether they attack, redirect, or negotiate.

second_order: keeping flag work in one organising thread
theme_note: Members and moderators redirect duplicates, use or replace a sticky, propose a dedicated subreddit, and later close the finished planning thread.

second_order: planning to make r/singapore look like r/malaysia
theme_note: People develop a future subreddit April Fools disguise through examples, redirects, a copied daily thread, and proposed moderator collaboration; it is separate from the canvas.

second_order: celebrating and closing the flag effort
theme_note: People announce progress or completion, congratulate and thank helpers, recount completion, and mark the canvas or sticky as finished.

second_order: guarding and repairing flags pixel by pixel
theme_note: People place or fix pixels, protect a heart, answer guard duty, contact painters, seek repair scripts, and recruit defenders.
People ask Malaysian helpers, exchange thanks, coordinate a shared heart, help repair neighbouring work, and display or joke about the joined flags.
